final_message:
The bug was in `Engine.refund` in `billing/engine.py`. It called `refunds.refund_invoice(invoice_id, self.ctx, reason)`, but the function's signature is `(ctx, invoice_id, reason)`. The invoice ID string ended up in the `ctx` slot, which caused `'str' object has no attribute 'store'`. I swapped the arguments.

I added your test as `tests/test_reports.py`. The full suite passes with it (25 tests).

I wrote `answer.json` as `{"file": "engine.py", "function": "refund"}`. It doesn't show in `git status`, so it may be gitignored.

steps.command: cat billing/reports.py && grep -n "def refund" -A30 billing/*.py | head -80

sed -i 's/refunds.refund_invoice(invoice_id, self.ctx, reason)/refunds.refund_invoice(self.ctx, invoice_id, reason)/' billing/engine.py && echo '{"file": "engine.py", "function": "refund"}' > answer.json && cat >> tests/test_reports.py <<'EOF'
EOF
git status --short; grep -rn "refund_invoice(" billing | grep -v "def "; .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

ls tests; git status --short; cat >> tests/test_reports.py <<'EOF'
EOF
git status --short

cat > tests/test_reports.py <<'EOF'
from billing import reports


def test_revenue_between_nets_credit_notes(world):
    cus = world.customer()
    world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 1)])
    [inv] = world.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    world.engine.refund(inv["id"])
    assert reports.revenue_between(world.ctx, inv["paid_at"], inv["paid_at"] + 1) == {"usd": 0}
EOF
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5; git status --short
